newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Few Beijing Ent orders placed before bell.
newsitem.headline: Few Beijing Ent orders placed before bell.

text.p: Few investors interested in buying shares in red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises appear to have listed their orders with the exchange in the hour prior to the opening of trading, brokers said.
"We do not trade in the grey market so we have no orders to put in," said a broker in the institutional sales department of a large British house.

In a move viewed as tacit recognition of a grey market, the stock exchange had asked brokers to report all trades in Beijing Enterprises concluded off the market to the exchange between 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. (0100 GMT and 0200 GMT).
Official trading in the share started at 10 a.m.
"With this move, the stock exchange has admitted that there is a grey market in the stock," said a broker at Asia Equity.
Under exchange rules, off-system trades, usually block trades between institutional investors, must be reported within the first 15 minutes of trading on the following day.
"We have a few orders, but people are going to wait for the open," said Geoff Galbraith, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities. "There is going to be a lot of trading in the first 15 minutes."

To alleviate pressure on its computer system in the first 15 minutes, the exchange said on Wednesday it would provide an input service for off-system trades to cope with heavy traffic when Beijing Enterprises Holdings started trading on Thursday.
The exchange said it would announce the size and turnover of trades made under the arrangement on the exchange news section at around 10.15 a.m. (0215 GMT).
In the first 15 minutes of trade, the share hit a high of HK$45.00 then eased to trade at HK$40.00 on heavy turnover of HK$802.86 million.
The red chip company's offer of 150 million new shares was 1,276 times oversubscribed.
